claim: The backfill/live-ingestion race is declared solved by 'recompute windows from source records at write time' but is not: an article scored after the backfill reads a window and fanned out live before the backfill writes it is clobbered (lost, unrecoverable because the analyzed gate blocks re-fanout); an article inside the backfill's read set whose live fanout lands after the backfill's write is double-counted. Both orderings are possible. SC-004 then contradicts reality: a repair re-run after such a race WOULD change bucket values, so either SC-004 fails or the race damage is kept
evidence: spec.md edge case 4 vs FR-004/SC-004; live fanout is unconditional ADD on the same keys (fanout.py:268), backfill write is wholesale recompute; analyzed gate handler.py:176,340 forecloses re-fanout of lost contributions
proposed_resolution: Specify the concurrency protocol: pause ingestion during backfill (A5 already requires operator go), or backfill only windows strictly older than a settle horizon (e.g. now minus 2x resolution), and re-scope SC-004 to quiesced conditions

claim: FR-006's amendment list is incomplete: MODELING.md's 'Re-running inference is not supported' section states 'There is no replay, rescore or backfill path in src/' and 'The mechanism does not [exist]' - the feature builds exactly that mechanism and the spec never amends or even mentions this section. SC-005 then defines success as 'the FR-006 list greps clean', equating completeness with the incomplete list, so SC-005 can pass while CANON still carries a falsified statement. Also missed: api_v2.py's module docstring already falsely claims 'Historical data backfill ... async pattern with job tracking' (no such function exists), which becomes actively misleading once a real backfill ships by a different mechanism
evidence: docs/MODELING.md:83-91; spec.md FR-006 lists only score-is-a-probability, SERVICE-SHAPE output-schema, README confidence wording, two handler docstrings; src/lambdas/dashboard/api_v2.py:8,21 vs its actual exports (get_sentiment_by_tags, get_trend_data, get_articles_by_tags only)
proposed_resolution: Add MODELING.md:83-91 and the api_v2.py docstring to FR-006; reword SC-005 so the grep target is 'statements the shipped behavior falsifies', with the FR-006 list as a floor, not the definition

claim: Context promises the change makes existing consumers correct ('every consumer - dashboard thresholds, chart axes, color ramps, digest labeling, the dormant alert evaluator - was built for signed aggregated values') but two named consumers never read buckets: the digest aggregates per-article records (and reads a 'sentiment_score' field that does not exist on stored items, so it is always 0.0/neutral), and SSE per-ticker aggregates average per-article unsigned 'score'. FR-008 explicitly excludes per-article consumers, so digest labeling stays broken and SSE streams unsigned ticker aggregates next to signed buckets after shipping. SC-006's 'return successfully' cannot catch semantic incoherence
evidence: digest_service.py:327 item.get('sentiment_score', 0) - field absent per MODELING.md:31 and analysis write set handler.py:326-329; digest thresholds :346-351 unreachable on 0.0; polling.py:185-210 averages per-article score (unsigned per FR-008) into TickerAggregate.score while :216-288 serves signed buckets on the same stream
proposed_resolution: Amend the Context to name digest and SSE per-ticker aggregates as explicitly NOT fixed (or pull them in scope); strengthen SC-006 to assert semantic consistency, not just 2xx

claim: Accumulation mechanism mismatch: the loud-failure edge case targets BatchWriteItem unprocessed items, but FR-002 accumulation cannot use BatchWriteItem (PutRequest replaces wholesale), forcing the UpdateItem path whose real failure modes the spec never covers. The existing candidate write_fanout_with_update issues 4 non-atomic UpdateItem calls per bucket x 6 resolutions; a crash mid-bucket leaves count/sum incremented but high/low/label_counts not, and it never updates avg at all, while every consumer reads bucket.avg
evidence: fanout.py:258-269 update expr ADDs count/sum, never SETs avg; fanout.py:330-336 separate label call; fanout.py:365-451 separate high/low calls; consumers read avg at dashboard/sentiment.py:329,626 and ohlc.py:1071; spec.md edge case 'Partial batch-write failures' names the wrong mechanism
proposed_resolution: Rewrite the edge case for the UpdateItem path; add an FR for partial-update failure observability and for maintaining avg (or have readers derive avg from sum/count); require single-call or crash-consistent accumulation design at plan time

claim: Fanout failure is observable but permanently unrecoverable, and the spec promotes neither property to a requirement: handler swallows every per-ticker fanout exception (warning + TimeseriesFanoutErrors metric, Lambda still succeeds), and the analyzed gate then forecloses any retry, so the contribution is lost forever. Today that loses one overwrite; under FR-002 it silently biases a population aggregate. FR-007's test list covers no failure path, and the loud-failure edge case is not an FR
evidence: handler.py:482-491 catch-all per ticker; handler.py:502-503 metric only; gate handler.py:176,340; spec FR-007 lists hop/accumulation/sign/idempotency only
proposed_resolution: Add an FR: fanout failures must be observable AND recoverable (e.g. failed tickers recorded so the FR-004 backfill, run for that window, repairs them - recompute-from-source already heals this class); include at least one failure-path test in FR-007

claim: FR-004 as written ('every bucket whose full window lies inside the retention horizon') obligates recreating fine-resolution buckets whose own TTLs expired long ago: 1m TTL is 6h, 5m 12h, 15m 24h, 30m 3d, 1h 7d, so a 30-day backfill would write ~43k dead 1m buckets per ticker with TTLs already in the past, and live data shows expired items linger rather than vanish. A4 acknowledges the tension ('mostly age out') but the MUST does not
evidence: models.py:57-65 ttl_seconds map; scan 2026-08-05: 18 items past TTL still present; resolution histogram of live table is 6127 of 7843 items at 24h, confirming fine resolutions age out
proposed_resolution: Scope FR-004 to buckets whose computed TTL is still in the future (equivalently: window newer than now minus resolution TTL), making A4's practical claim the actual requirement

claim: Zero-trust gap the feature makes worse: bucket SK derives from publisher-controlled article timestamps with no validation, and live data proves abuse-shaped inputs occur (buckets at 2017-12-19 and future 2026-08-06 exist in preprod). Today a mis-dated article overwrites one bucket visibly; under FR-002 accumulation it permanently skews a population aggregate with no removal path, and the FR-004 backfill windows on the same untrusted timestamps
evidence: handler.py:459 parses message timestamp verbatim into fanout; fanout.py:51 floor_to_bucket(score.timestamp); live scan 2026-08-05: AAPL#24h SK 2017-12-19T00:00:00+00:00 and SK 2026-08-06T00:00:00+00:00 both present
proposed_resolution: Add an FR bounding acceptable bucket timestamps (reject or clamp article timestamps in the future or older than retention) before accumulation ships; state the residual risk in the spec

claim: The backfill is a live-data mutation with no specified execution identity, credentials, or audit trail. Spec names no role (least privilege would be Query on sentiment-items plus write on sentiment-timeseries, nothing else), so the default becomes an operator's broad personal credentials; DynamoDB data-plane calls are not in CloudTrail unless data events are explicitly enabled, and no FR requires the run to record who/when/what-windows/how-many-buckets, so the mutation is unattributable after the fact
evidence: spec.md FR-004/A5 silent on identity, credentials, logging; iam/main.tf has no backfill principal; no CloudTrail data-event config in infrastructure/terraform
proposed_resolution: Add to FR-004: backfill runs under a named scoped role and emits a run manifest (start/end, window, per-resolution bucket counts, failures) to a log the operator keeps; owner explicitly accepts or declines CloudTrail data events

claim: Write-path threat surface the spec should state: bucket writers today are the analysis role AND the ingestion role, and the ingestion grant (BatchWriteItem/PutItem/UpdateItem on the timeseries table) is dormant - ingestion contains zero timeseries code. A poisoned bucket flows to dashboard responses (Pydantic clamps to [-1,1]; an out-of-range avg raises, which get_ticker_sentiment_history does not catch). Pre-existing, but a spec changing bucket write semantics is the right place to name the writers
evidence: iam/main.tf:113-132 ingestion_timeseries write grant; grep of src/lambdas/ingestion/ for TIMESERIES_TABLE/write_fanout/timeseries returns nothing; unvalidated construction path dashboard/sentiment.py:626-632 sits outside its try block
proposed_resolution: Note the writer set in the spec's context; recommend dropping the dormant ingestion grant as an adjacent one-line hardening (separate change, owner call)

claim: SC-003 is partially outside the feature's control: 'at least one negative or neutral labeled day' in the trailing 30 days of a high-volume ticker depends on the news cycle; a genuinely positive month fails the criterion with zero defects. Separately the '359 sampled buckets' marker should be restated as a re-runnable measurement so it cannot read as current evidence later
evidence: re-measurement 2026-08-05: 7843/7843 buckets count=1, 0 negative avg (premise currently true); SC-003 wording in spec.md
proposed_resolution: Split SC-003: the guaranteed part (count>1 on multi-article days, signed values present) stays a criterion; the label-mix part becomes a spot-check with a fallback (synthetic article per constitution's compute-expected-values rule). Replace the 359-sample citation with the scan command and its dated result

claim: FR-002 pins open/close to arrival order, but the backfill necessarily recomputes in article-timestamp order, so the first backfill run rewrites live-accumulated buckets' open/close/sources ordering even with no new data, and the table ends with mixed OHLC semantics (live buckets arrival-ordered, backfilled buckets timestamp-ordered). SC-004's 'byte-identical' only holds between backfill runs, which the spec does not say
evidence: FR-002 'open/close follow arrival order' vs FR-004 recompute-from-source; sources ordering via list_append at fanout.py:266
proposed_resolution: Define one ordering basis (article timestamp) for both paths, or state that backfilled windows switch to timestamp order and scope SC-004 to backfill-vs-backfill comparison

claim: Bucket 'sources' semantics are undefined under accumulation: live data stores per-article dedup ids ('dedup:<hash>') while models.py documents 'Unique data sources', list_append never dedupes, and the dashboard source filter (startswith 'tiingo'/'finnhub') can never match dedup ids. Accumulation makes the list grow per article and multiplies the drift; the spec's Key Entities lists 'sources' without saying what it holds after the change
evidence: live scan items carry sources [dedup:...]; models.py:124 'Unique data sources'; fanout.py:266 unconditional list_append; filter dashboard/sentiment.py:623 startswith(source)
proposed_resolution: Define sources under accumulation (either provider names deduped, or drop the attribute) in the spec's Key Entities and amend models.py's description in the FR-006 sweep
